title: Uniform derived evaluation bound for classical finite coefficient module sheaves
statement:
Let $k$ be a finite or algebraically closed field, $\ell$ a prime invertible in $k$, and $A$ a finite commutative ring with $\ell^aA=0$ for some integer $a\geq1$. Let $X$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme and $w:W\to X$ an affine étale object of its small étale site [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Work in a common larger universe in which the sites are small [def-weil-size-convention]. Put $d_X=\dim X$ if $X\ne\varnothing$ and $d_X=0$ if $X=\varnothing$, and put $e_X=2d_X+1$, with topological Krull dimension as in [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Use constant ring sheaves $A_T$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and ordinary left module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Regard $W$ also as an object of $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Call an $A_X$-module sheaf $H$ on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ classical when for every small cofiltered affine étale presentation $U=\varprojlim_iU_i$ over $X$, the canonical map $\varinjlim_iH(U_i)\to H(U)$ is an isomorphism of $A$-modules [sk-def-pe-classical-definition]. Define $E_W(H)=H(W)$ as an $A$-module by restriction of scalars along the constant-section map $A\to A_X(W)$. Define $R^qE_W$ by applying $E_W$ to an injective resolution in module sheaves on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ and taking its degree-$q$ cohomology [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Then, for every classical $H$ and every integer $q>e_X$,
$$R^qE_W(H)=0.$$
The bound is uniform over all affine étale $W\to X$ and all classical module sheaves $H$, without constructibility or finite generation.

source.place: Fixed-degree truncation: transfer of the étale bound to all classical module sheaves and identification with ambient-site evaluation; Stacks Tag 099W (proetale-lemma-compare-cohomology) and Tag 03F3 (sites-cohomology-lemma-cohomology-of-open).

proof.text: The sites in the statement are small in the chosen common larger universe. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck] to their constant ring sheaves and then [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. Thus the module-sheaf categories on $X_{\mathrm{ét}}$, $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$, $W_{\mathrm{ét}}$ and $W_{\mathrm{proét}}$ have enough injectives. Let $H$ be classical. Since $A$ is a discrete commutative ring, the equivalence onto classical modules in [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules] gives an étale $A_X$-module sheaf $G$ and an isomorphism $H\cong\nu_X^*G$. No finite-generation or constructibility property of $G$ is asserted or needed.

source.place: Essential image paragraph; existence of module resolutions as in Stacks injectives.tex Tag 079Q (remark-existence-D)

proof.text: Write $G|_W(V\to W)=G(V\to W\to X)$. For the étale morphism $w$, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] identifies abelian inverse image with this restriction, naturally in the sheaf. By [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image], inverse image of constant-$A$ modules has that underlying abelian inverse image and carries each constant scalar to the same scalar. Naturality of the restriction isomorphism with respect to each scalar endomorphism $a:G\to G$ therefore makes it $A$-linear: its two composites with multiplication by $a$ agree. Hence $w_{\mathrm{ét}}^{-1}G\cong G|_W$ as constant-$A$ module sheaves. Apply [lem-sfb-etale-module-affine-bound] to this $G$ and the given $W\to X$. Its field, prime, finite ring, annihilator, finite-type and affine étale hypotheses are precisely those of the item, and its $d_X,e_X$ conventions are identical. For every $q>e_X$ this gives $H_A^q(W_{\mathrm{ét}},G|_W)=0$.

source.place: Fixed-degree truncation, étale sheaf-bound input; restriction as in Stacks etale-cohomology.tex Tag 03S2 and sites.tex Tag 00YV

proof.text:
Regard $G$ as the complex $G[0]$. Apply the affine formula of [sk-prop-sf-comparison] with coefficient ring $A$ and with the presentation $W=\varprojlim_{i\in\{*\}}W$: the category has one object and only its identity, and its sole term is the given affine étale object. It is small, nonempty and cofiltered, its limit is $W$, and the opposite filtered colimit is just its single value. The formula consequently gives an isomorphism in the derived category of $A$-modules
$$R\Gamma(W_{\mathrm{proét}},(\nu_X^*G)|_W)\cong R\Gamma(W_{\mathrm{ét}},G|_W).$$
Here the input is bounded below because it is concentrated in degree zero; the comparison imposes no constructibility or finite-generation condition. On either site, clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] computes these right-derived section objects by evaluating a bounded-below injective resolution of the displayed sheaf. Their degree-$q$ cohomology is therefore the module cohomology used in step 2. Combining the comparison with $H|_W\cong(\nu_X^*G)|_W$ from step 1 and taking degree $q>e_X$ gives $H_A^q(W_{\mathrm{proét}},H|_W)=0$.

source.place: Affine formula paragraph, specialized to the constant one-object presentation; Stacks proetale.tex Tag 099W (lemma-compare-cohomology)

proof.text: The morphism $w$ is, as fixed in the statement, an object of $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-restriction-injectives], $W_{\mathrm{proét}}$ is its slice, and restriction of constant-coefficient module sheaves is exact and preserves injectives. Choose $H\to J^\bullet$ an injective module resolution on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Its restriction is then an injective resolution of $H|_W$ on $W_{\mathrm{proét}}$. At the final object $W\to W$, the restricted complex has terms $(J^n|_W)(W)=J^n(W)$ and the same differentials. The constant $A$-actions also coincide, since both act by restricting the constant scalar $a\in A$ to $W$. Thus the complex computing $R^qE_W(H)$ is literally the complex computing $H_A^q(W_{\mathrm{proét}},H|_W)$. The vanishing in step 3 proves $R^qE_W(H)=0$. The argument works separately for every affine étale $W$ with the unchanged bound $e_X$, so it proves the stated uniform assertion, including empty $X$ or $W$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q29-8394cd28b (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item, all 4 steps and every cited statement in full; review written to review.md. Step 1: lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck and lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives give enough injectives on the four small sites. det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules (any discrete commutative ring) gives H ≅ ν^*G with no finiteness condition. Step 2: lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction(1) gives the restriction isomorphism. lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image keeps the same constant scalars; A-linearity from naturality is elementary. lem-sfb-etale-module-affine-bound has the same k, ℓ, A, ℓ^aA=0, W and d_X/e_X conventions as the item. Step 3: the affine formula of sk-prop-sf-comparison with K=G[0] (bounded below) and the one-object cofiltered presentation (W is affine and étale, so a pro-étale affine). Clause (2) of lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective links RΓ to injective resolutions. Only the bounded-below comparison is used, never the unbounded one, so there is no circularity with lem-sfb-unbounded-site-comparison. The cycle check is clean. Step 4: lem-weil-pbc-proetale-restriction-injectives applies because objects of X_proét are weakly étale; it matches Stacks 03F3 (sites-cohomology l.608). This is the input of the Fixed-degree truncation paragraph, lines 16-26 of the main-20261015 unit proof. Small cases: algebraically closed field (true cd 0 ≤ 1), F_q (cd 1, nothing claimed at q=1), empty X/W, non-finitely-generated G. The statement is true and not weakened. No new nodes and no duplicates (det-pe-unbounded-classical-bounds(1) is abelian cohomology on U_proét, not module-valued evaluation on the ambient site). Batch-5 flag on lem-sfb-etale-module-affine-bound: in the closure of every proof_dep, the only sec-poincare-duality node is lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change. That node is a Mathlib leaf saying separated + finite type is stable under base change, a general scheme fact. It is not a step of the trace formula or of Poincaré duality, and neither assumption states it or the cohomological-dimension bound it feeds. No closure meets sec-trace-formula. So the citation is genuinely outside the assumptions. I accept the six generic tool_uses as declared. No SGA. No changes.
